sources.origin: Reuters report on T-Mobile Q2 2026 outlook

claims.claim: Independent reporting on Q2 says T-Mobile raised adjusted free-cash-flow guidance to $18.4B-$18.8B while warning premium-plan migration could temporarily reduce Q3 postpaid account additions and increase churn; this creates a clear cash-flow-versus-retention execution test.

risks: higher pricing may pressure churn and net adds
wireless saturation raises sensitivity to execution misses
contradictions: Higher free-cash-flow expectations coexist with a near-term churn/account-growth warning; monetization quality should be judged on retained lifetime value rather than price increases alone.
unknowns: duration of premium-plan migration churn effect
incremental return from fiber and adjacent broadband investment

recommendation.reason: Independent corroboration converts Q2 narrative into explicit FCF and retention checkpoints.
